clue.text: With difficulty, one respects things everyone knows

indicators.note: letters handled with difficulty are forced awkwardly into a fresh order

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to admire facts that are common knowledge anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is supposedly confidential information that is in fact widely known.

clue.text: Old-fashioned part of wheel's rotation finally very loud?

parts.note: out of fashion, dated
a rod joining hub to rim

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: final letter of rotation

explanation.surface: A spinning wheel's dated spoke makes a terribly noisy rattle as it turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: outspoken means frank rather than noisy, but such views are loudly voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: An outspoken person states opinions boldly and openly, figuratively loud in expressing them.

clue.text: Unknown figure is elevated in style of heavenly regions

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word up reads it from bottom to top
placed in means set inside another word

parts.note: elan is flair or style
Y is an algebraic unknown
is read upwards

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure is lifted up in the manner of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the Greek paradise for heroes, so Elysian describes blissful heavenly regions.

clue.text: Exceedingly wily, imprisoning rebellious soldiers, …

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut inside, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: sly means cunning
up in arms, in revolt
Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A cunning figure has locked up some mutinous troops, and the story continues.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, which also starts with soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremely means to the highest degree, an intensifying synonym of exceedingly.

clue.text: … soldiers run to be caught by police

indicators.note: being caught by something means being held within it

parts.note: informal word for police
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the troops flee only to be arrested by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military unit of soldiers, such as an army formation.

clue.text: Expression of self, one finally achieved with post-death message

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before

parts.note: last letter of one
got means obtained or achieved
Rest In Peace, the gravestone message

explanation.surface: Someone finally achieves fame and leaves a message after dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity pursued to boost self-importance, an indulgent display of oneself.

clue.text: Barely filled tin after inserting stone? On the contrary

indicators.note: inserting puts one word inside another
the contrary of the stated order swaps which word goes inside the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A can holds barely anything after a stone is pushed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary reverses the stated insertion: the stone is not put into the tin, the tin goes into the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means hardly sufficient, so something scant is barely filled out.

clue.text: Vaguely observed international judge going round Italy

parts.note: INT is a standard abbreviation for international

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: a judge hears a case
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A global referee circling Italy was only dimly noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is sensed vaguely all around, rumoured or felt but not plainly seen.

clue.text: Very close, though filling wide area

indicators.note: filling means sitting inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Things are very near even while they occupy a vast space.
explanation.definitionFit: A dear friend is an intimate one, very close in affection.

clue.text: Cracked like cracknel?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: full of nuts, as cracknel, a brittle nut sweet, often is

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is playful: cracknel is a crisp brittle confection, often made with nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both slang for crazy and literally containing or tasting of nuts.

clue.text: Servant concealing crime in church building

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
the crime of deliberately setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A household servant is hiding some wrongdoing within a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest, a building belonging to the church.

clue.text: Pleasure has to be taking in quiet trees

indicators.note: taking something in means admitting it inside, so the first word surrounds the rest

parts.note: taken as written
P, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
pines are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Enjoyment is found by absorbing the peace of a silent forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Happiness is a state of contentment and joy, close in sense to pleasure.

clue.text: Men going both ways holding front of this spinning device

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the paired words surround a letter
travelling in both directions means the word is read once backwards as well as forwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, read backwards

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of this
OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Workers moving in two directions grip the front of a spinning machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The men are read twice, once each way, making a palindrome round the central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter or engine.

clue.text: Question expert posed about neutron, sceptically

parts.note: to question is to ask

indicators.note: placed around something, so the word is set either side of a letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert
N is the symbol for neutron

explanation.surface: Someone asks a specialist about a subatomic particle and gets a doubtful response.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard with suspicion or doubt, so the adverb fits a sceptical attitude.

clue.text: Mozart symphony about to be returned after Judge finished with it

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
time is up when it is finished
taken as written
RE, about or concerning, reversed

explanation.surface: A judge has had enough of a famous symphony and wants it returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 41 in C major is universally nicknamed the Jupiter.

clue.text: A lot of sackcloth offering a thrill in an obvious way?

indicators.note: a lot of but not all means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: jute is the coarse fibre of sacking
tingly describes a thrilled sensation

explanation.surface: Wearing much sackcloth gives an obvious kind of thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a stretch: things that jut out stick out, and so are conspicuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Jutting things protrude and stand out, so acting jutting-ly is being conspicuous.

clue.text: Tout Seine, after translation, to become German

definitions.note: the answer is a verb meaning to make or become German

indicators.note: translation turns words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: French words for the whole Seine are translated into German.
explanation.walkthrough: Tout Seine looks French, inviting a real translation, but the letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Teutonise means to make or become Germanic in character, from the ancient Teutons.

clue.text: Deal with again? Deal with her afresh around noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding something placed inside
doing something afresh means starting anew, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Someone asks to revisit a matter, so deal with her again around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the phrase deal with, and the wordplay starts with the word deal as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehandle is to handle again, and handle means deal with.

clue.text: Fugitive advanced into part of airport

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: the strip where aircraft take off and land
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: An escaped criminal has made it onto an airport's grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway is a person who has fled or escaped, so it serves as a noun synonym for fugitive.

clue.text: Seasonal entertainment used to be a sea voyage

parts.note: past tense of to be
a sail is a trip by boat

explanation.surface: A Christmas festivity once consisted of a trip by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is traditional Christmas-time revelry, drinking spiced ale and carolling from house to house.

clue.text: Excessive ability holding doctor back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end
holding something means keeping it inside

parts.note: a deft touch is a skill or ability
MO, medical officer, read backwards

explanation.surface: A skilled practitioner is said to be keeping a doctor in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much is an idiom for an excessive amount, more than can be borne.

clue.text: Old and mean but not at first too old

indicators.note: not at first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the mean is the arithmetical average

explanation.surface: Someone elderly and stingy, though not originally, is now past it.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-age describes someone older than a permitted limit, beyond the right age.

clue.text: Soporific plant left world leader losing power

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: acronym for President of the United States
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A sleep-inducing plant has left a global leader drained of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer the lotus fruit induced dreamy forgetfulness, so the plant is proverbially sleep-inducing.

clue.text: Story about fellow would be biography

indicators.note: about means placed around something else

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A tale about a man would amount to an account of his life.
explanation.definitionFit: A Life is a written biography, as in a Life of Johnson.

clue.text: Suggestion burying uncovered bulb will produce flower

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so first and last letters go

parts.note: middle letters of bulb

explanation.surface: Advice to plant an unwrapped bulb so a bloom appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: Cat's important role, secondarily in economy

parts.note: main means chief or important

indicators.note: placed in means put inside another word

parts.note: a standard abbreviation for economy or economics

indicators.note: secondarily points to the second letter of the preceding word

parts.note: second letter of role

explanation.surface: A cat plays a key part, though only a supporting one, in saving money.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maine Coon is a large long-haired breed of domestic cat from New England.

clue.text: Wanders over, entering site of battle

indicators.note: entering means going inside

parts.note: Mons in Belgium, site of a First World War battle
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone roams across a historic battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon about is to wander around listlessly or dreamily.

clue.text: Be surrounded by everyone in family on arriving at last

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: informal shortening of family
all means everyone
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: final letter of arriving

explanation.surface: Someone finally arrives and finds themselves with the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall among people, as in thieves, is an idiom for ending up in their company.

clue.text: A cross and diamonds removed from clock face, indicating rotation?

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
X is shaped like a cross
the face of a clock
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone takes a cross and gems off a clock face, as though showing it turning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: an axis is what something rotates about.
explanation.definitionFit: Axial relates to an axis, the line about which a body turns, hence suggestive of rotation.

clue.text: Tyres openly moulded in synthetic material

indicators.note: moulded means shaped into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Tyres made in the open from some kind of artificial substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Polystyrene is a synthetic plastic polymer, used for packaging and insulation.
